_about: Best-known Gospel and Old Testament journeys: each step tied to the place it happens; places the text never mentions removed; missing story moments added.

steps.label: Rameses to Succoth
steps.copy: Israel sets out from Rameses on foot, a great company leaving Egypt.

steps.label: Toward the sea
steps.copy: The Lord has them turn back and camp by the sea, where escape looks impossible.

steps.label: Through the sea
steps.copy: The waters part, Israel crosses on dry ground, and the sea returns over Pharaoh's army.

steps.label: Marah and Elim
steps.copy: Bitter water at Marah is made sweet; at Elim there are twelve springs and seventy palm trees.

steps.label: Mount Sinai
steps.copy: In the third month they camp in front of the mountain in the Wilderness of Sinai.

set.note: Luke names only the start and the end; the road between Nazareth and Bethlehem is not recorded.

steps.label: Face set toward Jerusalem
steps.copy: As the time of his being taken up draws near, Jesus resolutely sets out for Jerusalem.

steps.label: Beyond the Jordan
steps.copy: He goes into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan, and crowds gather to him again.

steps.label: Jericho
steps.copy: At Jericho he gives sight to a blind man and stays at the house of Zacchaeus.

steps.label: Arrival near Bethany
steps.copy: Climbing from Jericho, they come near Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives.

steps.label: Into Jerusalem
steps.copy: Riding a colt as crowds spread cloaks and branches, he enters Jerusalem and goes into the temple.

steps.label: Rejected at Nazareth
steps.copy: In his hometown synagogue the crowd turns on him and tries to throw him off a cliff.

steps.label: Water into wine
steps.copy: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus turns water into wine, the first of his signs.

steps.label: Base at Capernaum
steps.copy: He makes his home by the lake and begins to preach: repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.

steps.label: Calling the fishermen
steps.copy: Simon, Andrew, James and John leave their nets to follow him.

steps.label: Crossing to the other side
steps.copy: He stills a storm on the lake and frees a man possessed by many demons.

steps.label: Feeding the five thousand
steps.copy: Near Bethsaida, five loaves and two fish feed a great crowd, with twelve baskets left over.

set.note: Emmaus has several proposed sites. Luke 24:13 puts it about seven miles from Jerusalem, so the map uses el-Qubeibeh, one site at that distance.

steps.label: Walking and talking
steps.copy: Two disciples talk over everything that has happened as Jesus himself comes near, but they don't recognize him.

steps.label: Opening the Scriptures
steps.copy: Beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he explains what was written about himself.

steps.label: Known in the breaking of bread
steps.copy: At the table he breaks the bread; their eyes are opened, and he vanishes from their sight.

steps.label: Back to Jerusalem
steps.copy: That same hour they return to Jerusalem and find the Eleven saying, “The Lord has indeed risen and has appeared to Simon!”

set.note: Joppa and Nineveh are known; where the storm struck and where Jonah was put ashore are not recorded.

steps.label: Sailing from Joppa
steps.copy: Running from the Lord, Jonah pays the fare and boards a ship bound for Tarshish.

steps.label: The storm and the fish
steps.copy: A great storm rises; Jonah is thrown overboard and swallowed by a great fish.

steps.label: Preaching in Nineveh
steps.copy: Sent a second time, Jonah goes to Nineveh; the city believes God and turns from its evil.

set.note: Matthew says only that the Magi came 'from the east'; their homeland and road are not recorded.

points.modern: east of Judea (Persia and Babylon are common guesses)

steps.label: Following the star
steps.copy: Magi from the east arrive in Jerusalem asking where the newborn king of the Jews is.

steps.label: Sent to Bethlehem
steps.copy: Herod sends them to Bethlehem and asks them to report back; the star goes ahead of them.

steps.label: Worship and gifts
steps.copy: They find the child with Mary, bow down to worship him, and offer gold, frankincense and myrrh.

steps.label: Home by another way
steps.copy: Warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they return to their country by another route.
